newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Shinpan leasing affiliate may get funds.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Shinpan leasing affiliate may get funds.

text.p: A non-listed leasing affiliate of Nippon Shinpan Co Ltd, Japan's largest consumer credit card company, said on Thursday it has mapped out a reconstruction plan but said creditors had not yet reached an agreement on it.

An official at Interlease Corp said the plan was currently being discussed between Nippon Shinpan and its four major creditors -- Sakura Bank, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, Sanwa Bank and the Taiyo Mutual Life Insurance Co.
"We have heard that the discussions are progressing positively," he said.
Financial sources said the plan calls for a total of 200 billion yen in supporting funds from Nippon Shinpan and the creditor financial institutions.
Interlease arranges loans for real-estate mortgages as well as leasing machine tools and transportation equipment.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Thursday that the balance of debt held by the leasing company amounts to some 860 billion yen. Problem loans at the company are estimated to be more than half of 400 billion yen it loaned out during the late 1980's bubble economic era of inflating land prices, it said.
